# 0. OVERVIEW & SETUP

This script builds the aggregated files for the Shiny dashboard. It
reads two files saved from Main Analysis Rmd:

- `data_analytic.rds`: the analytic sample (54 countries, WRD-based
  majority/minority status, negative outcome codes already set to NA).
  Used for descriptive tables.
- `dashboard_model_outputs.rds`: country-level adjusted gaps (stage 1),
  pooled meta-analysis results, VPCs, country indicators, and GRI/SHI
  moderation results. These are the numbers in the paper.

### Setup

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, countrycode)

# Inputs from the Main Analysis (not committed to the repository)
data          <- readRDS("data_analytic.rds")
model_outputs <- readRDS("dashboard_model_outputs.rds")

data %>% nrow()
data$country %>% n_distinct()                 # should be 54
data %>% count(religion_status, useNA = "ifany")
```

Helper functions

```{r helper-functions}
w_mean <- function(x, w) {
  keep <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(w) & w > 0
  if (sum(keep) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  sum(x[keep] * w[keep]) / sum(w[keep])
}

w_se <- function(x, w) {
  keep <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(w) & w > 0
  if (sum(keep) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  x <- x[keep]; w <- w[keep]
  n_eff <- sum(w)^2 / sum(w^2)          # Kish effective sample size
  m     <- sum(w * x) / sum(w)
  v     <- sum(w * (x - m)^2) / sum(w)  # weighted variance
  sqrt(v / n_eff)
}

tidy_religion <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    gsub("_", " ", .) %>%
    gsub("No [Dd]enomination", "No religious denomination", .) %>%
    gsub("^Jew$", "Jewish", .) %>%
    gsub("Ethnic religionist", "Ethnic religions", .) %>%
    gsub("Chinese folk religionist", "Chinese folk religions", .) %>%
    gsub("Other religion$", "Other", .)
}

outcome_labels <- c(
  life_satisfaction = "Life satisfaction (1–10)",
  happiness         = "Happiness (1–4)",
  health            = "Self-rated health (1–5)"
)
```

# 1. CHECK INPUTS

Majority/minority status was assigned in the Main Analysis code file
(majority = religion with \>50% of the national population, World
Religion Database). Here we only check the inputs are consistent with
each other.

```{r check-inputs}
# Outcomes should already be clean (no negative codes)
data %>%
  summarise(across(c(life_satisfaction, happiness, health),
                   list(min = ~ min(.x, na.rm = TRUE), max = ~ max(.x, na.rm = TRUE))))
stopifnot(min(data$life_satisfaction, na.rm = TRUE) >= 1,
          min(data$happiness,         na.rm = TRUE) >= 1,
          min(data$health,            na.rm = TRUE) >= 1)

# Same countries in the data and in the model outputs
countries_data   <- sort(unique(data$country))
countries_models <- sort(unique(model_outputs$country_estimates$country))
setdiff(countries_data, countries_models)   # should be empty
setdiff(countries_models, countries_data)   # should be empty

# Survey weights: replace missing/non-positive with 1
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    survey_weight   = if_else(is.na(survey_weight) | survey_weight <= 0, 1, survey_weight),
    religion_status = factor(religion_status, levels = c("Majority", "Minority"))
  )
```

World Religion Database shares

```{r wrd-shares}
religion_pct_map <- tibble(
  religion = c("Buddhist", "Chinese_folk_religionist", "Christian", "Confucianist",
               "Daoist", "Ethnic_religionist", "Hindu", "Jain", "Jew", "Muslim",
               "Shintoist", "Sikh", "Spiritist", "Other", "No_Denomination"),
  pct_var  = c("buddhist_pct", "chinese_folk_religionist_pct", "christian_pct",
               "confucianist_pct", "daoist_pct", "ethnic_religionist_pct",
               "hindu_pct", "jain_pct", "jew_pct", "muslim_pct", "shintoist_pct",
               "sikh_pct", "spiritist_pct", "other_religion_pct", "no_denomination_pct")
)

wrd_long <- data %>%
  distinct(country, across(all_of(religion_pct_map$pct_var))) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(religion_pct_map$pct_var),
               names_to = "pct_var", values_to = "wrd_share") %>%
  left_join(religion_pct_map, by = "pct_var") %>%
  select(country, religion, wrd_share)

# Checks: both should return nothing
wrd_long %>% count(country, religion) %>% filter(n > 1)
setdiff(unique(data$religion_wrd), religion_pct_map$religion)

country_majority <- data %>%
  distinct(country, majority_religion) %>%
  left_join(wrd_long, by = c("country", "majority_religion" = "religion")) %>%
  rename(majority_share = wrd_share)   # WRD national population %
```

Country sample checks

```{r country-check}
country_check <- data %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    n_total      = n(),
    n_majority   = sum(religion_status == "Majority"),
    n_minority   = sum(religion_status == "Minority"),
    pct_minority = 100 * n_minority / n_total,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(pct_minority)

country_check %>% print(n = Inf)
country_check %>% filter(n_minority < 30)   # flagged, not dropped: estimates will be imprecise
```

# 2. BUILD DASHBOARD TABLES

## Country lookup

```{r country-lookup}
country_lookup <- data %>%
  distinct(country) %>%
  mutate(iso3c = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", destination = "iso3c"))

country_lookup %>% filter(is.na(iso3c))   # should be empty
```

## Table 1: Religious composition by country

WVS sample share is survey-weighted; WRD share is the national
population %. Religious majority/minority status follows the WRD-based
classification.

```{r table-composition}
tbl_composition <- data %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  mutate(country_w = sum(survey_weight)) %>%
  group_by(country, religion_wrd, religion_status) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), n_w = sum(survey_weight),
            country_w = first(country_w), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(share = 100 * n_w / country_w) %>%
  left_join(wrd_long, by = c("country", "religion_wrd" = "religion")) %>%
  transmute(country,
            religion = tidy_religion(religion_wrd),
            n, share, wrd_share,
            status = as.character(religion_status)) %>%
  arrange(country, desc(share))

tbl_composition %>% slice_head(n = 10)
```

## Table 2: Outcome means by country and status (descriptive)

Survey-weighted, unadjusted means. These describe each group's level of
health & wellbeing; the gaps reported in the paper come from Table 3.

```{r table-means}
tbl_means <- data %>%
  select(country, religion_status, survey_weight,
         life_satisfaction, happiness, health) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(life_satisfaction, happiness, health),
               names_to = "outcome", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  group_by(country, outcome, religion_status) %>%
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    mean = w_mean(value, survey_weight),
    se   = w_se(value, survey_weight),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    lower = mean - 1.96 * se,
    upper = mean + 1.96 * se,
    outcome_label = outcome_labels[outcome]
  )

tbl_means %>% slice_head(n = 6)
```

## Table 3: Minority–majority gaps by country

`gap` is the **adjusted** gap from the paper's stage-1 country
regressions (survey-weighted, adjusted for age and sex, HC2 robust SEs);
these match the forest plots and maps. `gap_raw` is the unadjusted
difference in weighted means, kept for reference.

Negative values mean religious minorities score lower than the majority.

```{r table-gaps}
# Unadjusted (descriptive) gap
gaps_raw <- tbl_means %>%
  select(country, outcome, religion_status, mean, se, n) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = religion_status, values_from = c(mean, se, n)) %>%
  mutate(gap_raw       = mean_Minority - mean_Majority,
         gap_raw_se    = sqrt(se_Minority^2 + se_Majority^2),
         gap_raw_lower = gap_raw - 1.96 * gap_raw_se,
         gap_raw_upper = gap_raw + 1.96 * gap_raw_se)

# Adjusted gap (stage 1 of the meta-analysis)
gaps_adj <- model_outputs$country_estimates %>%
  transmute(country, outcome,
            gap       = estimate,
            gap_se    = std.error,
            gap_lower = estimate - 1.96 * std.error,
            gap_upper = estimate + 1.96 * std.error)

tbl_gaps <- gaps_adj %>%
  left_join(gaps_raw, by = c("country", "outcome")) %>%
  mutate(outcome_label = outcome_labels[outcome]) %>%
  left_join(country_lookup, by = "country") %>%
  left_join(country_majority, by = "country") %>%
  left_join(country_check %>% select(country, n_total, n_minority, pct_minority), by = "country") %>%
  left_join(model_outputs$country_indicators, by = "country") %>%
  mutate(majority_religion = tidy_religion(majority_religion))

# Check: one row per country x outcome
stopifnot(nrow(tbl_gaps) == n_distinct(tbl_gaps$country) * 3)

tbl_gaps %>%
  filter(outcome == "life_satisfaction") %>%
  arrange(gap) %>%
  select(country, majority_religion, gap, gap_lower, gap_upper, gap_raw) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

## Table 4: Pooled results (meta-analysis)

```{r table-pooled}
tbl_pooled <- model_outputs$meta_summary %>%
  left_join(model_outputs$vpc, by = "outcome") %>%
  mutate(outcome_label = outcome_labels[outcome])

tbl_pooled
```

## Table 5: Moderation by government restrictions and social hostilities

Simple effects are the minority–majority gap within each GRI/SHI
category (95% CIs, multiplicity-adjusted across categories). Interaction
terms are given for every country-level indicator (90% CIs, α = 0.10);
for GRI/SHI categories, each compares that category's gap with the Low
category.

```{r table-moderation}
tbl_simple_effects <- model_outputs$simple_effects %>%
  mutate(category = as.character(category),
         outcome_label = outcome_labels[outcome])

model_labels <- c(
  gri_cat   = "Government restrictions (category)",
  gri       = "Government restrictions (continuous)",
  shi_cat   = "Social hostilities (category)",
  shi       = "Social hostilities (continuous)",
  democracy = "Democracy index",
  gdp       = "Log GDP per capita",
  gini      = "Gini index"
)

tbl_interactions <- model_outputs$interactions %>%
  mutate(moderator = factor(model_labels[model], levels = model_labels),
         term = if_else(grepl("_category", term),
                        paste(gsub("gri_category|shi_category", "", term), "vs Low"),
                        "Per 1-unit increase"),
         outcome_label = outcome_labels[outcome]) %>%
  arrange(outcome, moderator) %>%
  select(outcome, outcome_label, model, moderator, term, estimate, se, ci_lb, ci_ub, p)

# Number of countries in each category (for the app's notes)
tbl_category_n <- model_outputs$country_indicators %>%
  pivot_longer(c(gri_category, shi_category), names_to = "index", values_to = "category") %>%
  filter(!is.na(category)) %>%
  mutate(index = if_else(index == "gri_category", "GRI", "SHI"),
         category = as.character(category)) %>%
  count(index, category, name = "n_countries")

tbl_simple_effects
tbl_interactions
tbl_category_n
```

## Table 6: Sex-stratified results

Country gaps for men and women separately (survey-weighted, adjusted for
age, HC2 robust SEs), the pooled gap for each sex (95% CI), and the
pooled difference between women and men (90% CI, α = 0.10).

```{r table-sex}
tbl_sex_country <- model_outputs$sex_country_estimates %>%
  transmute(country, outcome,
            sex       = if_else(sex_group == "Female", "Women", "Men"),
            gap       = estimate,
            gap_lower = estimate - 1.96 * std.error,
            gap_upper = estimate + 1.96 * std.error,
            outcome_label = outcome_labels[outcome])

tbl_sex_pooled <- model_outputs$sex_meta %>%
  mutate(sex = if_else(sex_group == "Female", "Women", "Men"),
         outcome_label = outcome_labels[outcome]) %>%
  select(outcome, outcome_label, sex, estimate, ci_lb, ci_ub, p, I2, k)

tbl_sex_diff <- model_outputs$sex_interaction_meta %>%
  mutate(outcome_label = outcome_labels[outcome])

tbl_sex_pooled
tbl_sex_diff
```

## Table 7: Missingness by status

Among respondents with at least one valid outcome. Minorities were more
likely to skip outcome items, so gaps may be conservative.

```{r table-missingness}
tbl_missing <- data %>%
  group_by(religion_status) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    pct_missing_ls     = round(100 * mean(is.na(life_satisfaction)), 1),
    pct_missing_happy  = round(100 * mean(is.na(happiness)), 1),
    pct_missing_health = round(100 * mean(is.na(health)), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

tbl_missing
```

# 3. SAVE AGGREGATED DATA FOR THE DASHBOARD

```{r save-dashboard-data}
dashboard_data <- list(
  composition    = tbl_composition,
  means          = tbl_means,
  gaps           = tbl_gaps,
  pooled         = tbl_pooled,
  simple_effects = tbl_simple_effects,
  interactions   = tbl_interactions,
  category_n     = tbl_category_n,
  sex_country    = tbl_sex_country,
  sex_pooled     = tbl_sex_pooled,
  sex_diff       = tbl_sex_diff,
  missingness    = tbl_missing,
  lookup         = country_lookup,
  meta = list(
    n_countries         = n_distinct(data$country),
    n_respondents       = nrow(data),
    n_majority          = sum(data$religion_status == "Majority"),
    n_minority          = sum(data$religion_status == "Minority"),
    majority_definition = "Religion with >50% of the national population (World Religion Database 2020)",
    gap_definition      = "Adjusted for age and sex; survey-weighted country regressions with HC2 robust SEs",
    models_saved_on     = model_outputs$saved_on,
    built_on            = Sys.Date()
  )
)

dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(dashboard_data, "data/dashboard_data.rds")

# Plain CSV of country-level gaps for download in the app
write_csv(dashboard_data$gaps, "data/country_gaps.csv")

dashboard_data$meta
```
